items.title: Fed could hike interest rates as U.S. inflation heats up
items.summary: A U.S. Federal Reserve interest-rate decision later this month may be a closer call than previously thought, traders bet on Wednesday, after U.S. Labor Department data showed consumer prices were up 3.7 per cent last month from a year earlier, well above the Fed’s two per cent target and moving in the wrong direction.

items.title: Gold drops over 1% as hot US inflation data boosts Fed hike bets
items.summary: US consumer prices increased in September, contributing to expectations of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. Following this inflation data, gold prices fell over 1% for the third consecutive session. The US dollar index also climbed, making gold more expensive for foreign investors. Market predictions indicate a 44% chance of a rate hike in October and a 95% chance in December.

items.title: US inflation rises to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices jump 9.1%
items.summary: US consumer inflation rose to 3.7 per cent in September from 3.4 per cent in August, driven largely by a sharp increase in gasoline prices, adding to concerns over persistent price pressures ahead of the Federal Reserve's next interest rate decision.

items.title: US inflation worsened last month to 3.7% in sign that prices remain elevated as midterm elections near
items.summary: U.S. inflation increased in September as consumers faced higher prices for essentials like gas and clothing. The consumer price index rose 3.7% compared to the previous year, indicating ongoing economic challenges. This rise in inflation has political implications ahead of the midterm elections, impacting public sentiment towards Republican lawmakers. Federal Reserve officials are closely monitoring trends to determine future interest rate decisions.

items.title: Inflation heats up in September
items.summary: Inflation heated up again in September as rising energy costs intensified price pressures, bolstering the Federal Reserve’s case for another interest-rate hike this year.

items.title: More expensive gas, semiconductors likely pushed up inflation in US last month
items.summary: Inflation in the United States is projected to increase to 3.6% in September from the previous month. This rise is attributed to factors such as continuous supply issues caused by the Iran war. The Federal Reserve is monitoring inflation data closely and may adjust interest rates accordingly. Several companies, including PepsiCo, have announced price increases to address rising costs.

items.title: Trump tariffs also caused 'Made in America' prices to go up, NY Fed finds
items.summary: Trump's tariffs contributed 2.9 percentage points to consumer goods inflation, according to Federal Reserve Bank of New York research. Energy prices add further pressure.
